Development notes"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"**Give your DSH agent hands inside the Chrome you are already using** — your logins, your tabs, your"},{"id":"p5s2","text":" session. Install once, no Connect button, ever."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"> **What it is:** a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that lets the model operate the Chrome you already"},{"id":"p6s2","text":" use: open pages, click, type, fill in forms, read pages, take screenshots and work across tabs, wit"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"h your existing logins.
>
> **Use it for:** "fill in this web form", "check this admin page for me","},{"id":"p6s4","text":" "screenshot this site", or anything else the model has to do inside a browser.
>
> **Install:** on "},{"id":"p6s5","text":"the DSH Plugins page, click Add plugin and enter `dsh-chrome-bridge` (an npm package), restart DSH, "},{"id":"p6s6","text":"then add the DSH Bridge extension from the Chrome Web Store. Needs macOS, Windows or Linux, Chrome 1"},{"id":"p6s7","text":"16+ and Node.js 18+."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"Every click flies a cursor to the target and labels what it is doing. It renders *inside the page*, "},{"id":"p7s2","text":"so it lands in screenshots too — you and the model look at the same picture."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## ✨ Why another browser bridge?"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"Every existing option makes you click something, every time:"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"| Option | What goes wrong |"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"| `chrome-devtools-mcp --autoConnect` | Chrome asks *"Allow remote debugging?"* on **every** connect"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"ion |
| Browser MCP (store extension) | You must click the extension icon → **Connect** on **every**"},{"id":"p11s3","text":" tab |
| WebSocket-based bridges | Open a TCP port and trust anything that can reach it |
| **dsh-ch"},{"id":"p11s4","text":"rome-bridge** | Nothing to click. Nothing listening on a port. |"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"Three things make the difference:"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"- 🔌 **Native messaging, not a port.** The extension talks to a local Node host over Chrome's native "},{"id":"p13s2","text":"messaging pipe; the CLI reaches the host through a `0600` Unix socket guarded by a token. No TCP por"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"t to scan, no origin to spoof.
- 🎯 **`chrome.debugger`, not injected scripts.** Clicks and keystroke"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"s are dispatched as real CDP `Input.*` events, so they carry a user gesture — popups open, focus wor"},{"id":"p13s5","text":"ks, and sites that reject synthetic events behave normally. Screenshots, network, console and raw CD"},{"id":"p13s6","text":"P come for free.
- 👀 **A cursor the human can see.** A translucent light-blue arrow with a "🌐 DSH" n"},{"id":"p13s7","text":"ame tag glides along a gentle arc to the target; the tag says what it is doing (click / type / drag "},{"id":"p13s8","text":"/ scroll) and each click leaves a soft ripple. It shares one style with the desktop cursor of dsh-ma"},{"id":"p13s9","text":"c-computer-use (solid there, with a monitor icon), so you can tell at a glance whether the work is i"},{"id":"p13s10","text":"n the browser or on the desktop. It sits above modals and fullscreen, and picks up where it was afte"},{"id":"p13s11","text":"r a navigation. Because it is rendered inside the page, **it appears in screenshots**."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"## 🏗 Architecture"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"**This repo ships no agent** — the agent above is DSH's own; we only give it hands."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"The extension ID is fixed by the public key embedded in `plugin/vendor/extension/manifest.json`, so "},{"id":"p17s2","text":"it is **identical on every machine** and the native-host registration never needs editing. The Web S"},{"id":"p17s3","text":"tore build has its own store-assigned ID; the host accepts both."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"## 🚀 Install"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"**The host ships inside the plugin package.** Adding the plugin copies the native host and the MV3 e"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"xtension into place and registers native messaging for you — no `git clone`, no `install.sh`, no `py"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"n into place and registers native messaging for you — no `git clone`, no `install.sh`, no `python3`."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"Requirements: **macOS, Windows or Linux**, **Google Chrome 116+**, **Node.js 18+**."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"### 👀 What you see while it works"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"- **Click the toolbar icon** for a live panel: whether Chrome ↔ local host ↔ DSH are connected, **wh"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"ich DSH sessions are driving which tabs** (jump to a tab, or release it with one click), the last ac"},{"id":"p23s3","text":"tions with their errors, a **pause switch** that makes the browser off-limits until you turn it back"},{"id":"p23s4","text":" on, and *copy diagnostics* for bug reports. The icon badge shows how many tabs are under control (`"},{"id":"p23s5","text":"!` = host down, `⏸` = paused).
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"## 🔒 Security"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"Be honest about what this is: **the extension can read and control every page you are logged into.**"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"- The bridge is **local-only**. Native messaging is a private pipe; the CLI socket is `0600` and add"},{"id":"p26s2","text":"itionally token-guarded. **It opens no network listener of its own** (the DSH settings card goes thr"},{"id":"p26s3","text":"ough DSH's built-in local web server; that route only accepts loopback, rejects cross-site requests,"},{"id":"p26s4","text":" and cannot resume control).
- Chrome shows a permanent *"… is debugging this browser"* banner while"},{"id":"p26s5","text":" attached. That banner is the point — you can always see that it is active.
- Anything that can alre"},{"id":"p26s6","text":"ady run as your user can read your Chrome profile; this does not widen that boundary. It does make i"},{"id":"p26s7","text":"t *convenient*, which is worth a thought before leaving an agent unattended.
- **Once the DSH plugin"},{"id":"p26s8","text":" is installed, the model drives your browser without asking.** Plugin tools run inside the DSH host "},{"id":"p26s9","text":"process, so they are *not* gated by the workspace sandbox or the approval prompts that guard `bash`."},{"id":"p26s10","text":" That is what "native" buys you — and it means an unattended agent holds your browser. Disable the p"},{"id":"p26s11","text":"lugin in the sidebar if you want that gate back.
- Detach any time: click **Cancel** on the banner, "},{"id":"p26s12","text":"or `cb detach <tab>`."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"## ⚠️ Limitations"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- **Windows and Linux support is new** — a daily CI run on GitHub's Windows and Linux machines insta"},{"id":"p28s2","text":"lls it, connects a real Chrome and reads a page, but it has not been used on a real person's PC yet."},{"id":"p28s3","text":" Please open an issue if something breaks. On Windows it also registers for Edge (untested).
- **`ch"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"rome://` pages are unreachable** — Chrome forbids injection there. Use a normal tab.
- An `alert()` "},{"id":"p28s5","text":"blocks the page: `cb info` warns you, `cb dialog accept` releases it.
- Chrome defers `alert()` in b"},{"id":"p28s6","text":"ackground tabs until the tab is focused.
- Without the Web Store, Chrome 137+ (no more `--load-exten"},{"id":"p28s7","text":"sion`) needs one manual load through `chrome://extensions`.
- The Web Store build lags the repo a li"},{"id":"p28s8","text":"ttle: new extension versions wait for store review."}],"truncated":true}
